newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-BECKER ENJOYS FLIGHT TO NIRVANA IN SAMPRAS DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER ENJOYS FLIGHT TO NIRVANA IN SAMPRAS DEFEAT.

text.p: Boris Becker brought 15,000 ecstatic Germans to their feet and flew into another world himself at the ATP world championship on Thursday with his second dramatic victory over Pete Sampras in less than a month.

The triple Wimbledon champion, who beat the world number one over five sets in last month's Stuttgart Open final, took a confident step towards the semifinals with a victory that the Hanover crowd and millions of Germans watching live on television will remember for a long time.

The first set of the round-robin red group match went to 12-10 in the tiebreak. Becker played some of the best tennis of his life to clinch the match in the second-set tiebreak, the thriller lasting two hours and nine minutes.

Becker said he had rarely been so high for a match. At times he admitted he needed to calm himself down, especially after the two players entered the arena to the music from the "Rocky" boxing movies.
"When I was waiting to come in and heard the Rocky music I was just about to make some boxing movements coming out. I was so pumped up. It was incredible," Becker said.
"I was covered in goosepimples. I felt just about to take off the ground and fly into Nirvana."

"But he is still the undisputed heavyweight champion. It is always a special moment in my life to beat him. It wasn't a grand slam final today. But I played at a level that I haven't reached for a long time."
Sampras, who destroyed Andre Agassi in his opening match, still has a chance to make it through to the last four in his final group match against Russian Yevgeny Kafelnikov on Friday.
He said he had given Becker an early birthday present by not taking his chances. The German turns 29 on Friday.
"I am upset that I had a lot of chances and got nothing out of it," Sampras said. "It is a tough loss to get over. I played well enough to win.

"I am getting a bit tired of playing Boris in Germany... It is not fun, " he joked. "It was like two heavyweights at it...I have no more presents for him. I gave him a present today...But I'm not out of it yet."
Becker has always had a special relationship with his fans that few sportsmen in the world can match.
He is like their favourite character in a soap opera. When he walks on court, they switch off from the real world and enjoy his high points and suffer his lows with him.
From the moment he appeared in the arena, the Hanover thousands chanted Becker's name like a football crowd and clapped his every move furiously.
Becker played with their emotions in a dramatic first set which lasted 71 minutes, a lot longer than most of the matches so far at the event.
The first eight games were tight. Then Becker had to pull out some of his best serves to save three sets points against him in the 10th game.
Then came the nail-biting tiebreak that gripped the crowd. Both players had several chances to take the decider.

It was Becker, however, who finally took his chance, hitting a superb forehand from the back of the court down the line to lead 11-10. The German then clinched the set in the next point when Sampras hit a forehand return into the net.
Sampras seemed to be pushing the match into a third set when he broke Becker's serve to take a 5-4 lead in the next set. But Becker broke back in the next game.
When the set went to another tiebreak Sampras seemed to lose his concentration and Becker quickly took a 4-1 lead.
The German set up match points with his 24th ace of the match, then clinched the tiebreak 7-4 with a superb backhand passing shot.
Earlier, in the white group Michael Chang beat Goran Ivanisevic 6-7 (8-10) 7-6 (7-5) 6-1.
